abstract: Molecular data for Colombian Hypostomus remain sparse, limiting assessments of species boundaries. We combined two mitochondrial markers (cox1 and D-loop) with morphological, morphometric, geographic, and taxonomic evidence to evaluate diversity among Colombian populations. Using ASAP, bPTP, and GMYC, cox1 recovered 16-17 Molecular Operational Taxonomic Units (MOTUs), whereas D-loop yielded 32-37, indicating finer mitochondrial lineage partitioning in D-loop that was not consistently mirrored by phenotypic differentiation. Because both markers belong to the same non-independent mitochondrial linkage group, congruence reflects partition stability rather than independent multi-locus support. High taxonomic-assignment support was obtained for H. holostictus, H. hondae, H. niceforoi, H. plecostomoides, H. oculeus, and H. weberi, whereas H. carinatus, H. hemicochliodon, and H. sculpodon received moderate support and H. wilsoni remained provisional because voucher-linked verification of the sequenced individuals was unavailable. Seven candidate lineages remain unresolved (G1, G2, and M3-M7); M8 was not counted among them because the examined specimens were morphologically compatible with H. hemicochliodon. Among these candidates, Hypostomus sp. G1 and G2 showed method-dependent mitochondrial partitioning and differences in selected morphometric characters relative to examined topotypic H. robinii. G2 also differed in pigmentation from examined H. rhantos, despite morphometric overlap. However, morphometric classification performance in Magdalena specimens and unresolved diagnostic boundaries do not provide sufficient evidence for recognizing G1 and G2 as distinct species. Mitochondrial delimitation patterns can reveal lineage partitioning and help identify taxonomic priorities, but should not be equated with species boundaries. Broader sampling, verified vouchers, and independent nuclear or genomic data are needed to evaluate these taxonomic hypotheses.
